analysis.title: September Payroll Preview: +60k Gain Likely
key_insights: Piper Sandler estimates September nonfarm payrolls rose +60k vs consensus +90k, down from August's +162k print.
Unemployment rate is expected to hold at 4.1%, the same as consensus.
ADP private employment rose +90k in September vs +75k consensus. August was +36k (revised down 2k). ADP's weekly employment tracker has also shifted higher.
Initial unemployment claims are extremely low and continuing claims are rangebound, which Piper says points to healthy job growth.
The employment diffusion index has hooked up, which Piper reads as hiring broadening across sectors.

August payrolls were boosted by state and local education hiring tied to summer-recess seasonal-adjustment difficulties. Piper expects that boost to reverse in September, which explains its below-consensus estimate.
A composite of regional Fed manufacturing future employment plans is near its cycle high, which points to stronger manufacturing hiring ahead.

Data center construction is boosting nonresidential construction employment. Residential construction employment is likely to stay weak given depressed homebuilder confidence and worsening affordability.
Piper estimates September average hourly earnings at +0.3% m/m (same as August), with y/y accelerating to 3.2% from 3.1%. Consensus is +0.3% m/m and 3.1% y/y.
Piper expects wage growth to steady, tracking stabilization in the JOLTS private quit rate, with potential for a reacceleration in 2027.

The Conference Board's Jobs Hard-Jobs Easy metric keeps climbing, suggesting consumers think unemployment is still trending higher. The covered unemployment rate (continuing claims divided by employees covered by state unemployment insurance) is a historically low 1.1%.
